subject: Modifying graph colors and visualising figure legends

messages.author: a64f316d2c410047
messages.subject: Modifying graph colors and visualising figure legends
parts:
Dear All,
I have just started to use Rattle. I generated some graphs (say boxplots) which are empty boxes. I would like to have some colors filled in the boxes. How can I get that?
I have a second question: I would also like to export (or atlease view) the figure legends. Is there any option on GUI or by command?
Thanks a lot in advance.
Ramesh

messages.author: a64f316d2c410047
messages.subject: Re: Modifying graph colors and visualising figure legends
parts:
I should make the question more clear, I will try to explain the problem again:

For example, with weather dataset, I can make box plot and I can also do correlation (spearman/pearson) that results in graphical output.
Now, for example, in correlation plot where it produces a plot containing circles( or angled ovoids) filled with gradient of blue to red colors. If I used that in publications, I must provide a legend explaining what do colors and shapes mean.

So, I want to visualise and export figure legends.

I hope I could make the question clear.

Ramesh

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Modifying graph colors and visualising figure legends
parts:
Rattle currently uses plotcorr() from ellipse. I am thinking to move to corrplot() from corrplot which includes a legend and arguably looks better. You can do the same by copying the code from the Rattle log tab into the R console to do the plotcorr(). Then

> install.packages("corrplot")
> library(corrplot)
> corrplot(crs$cor)

Similarly for any other plots generated by Rattle which do not do exactly what you want. Copy the code from the Rattle Log tab into the R Console to replicate the plot, then start fine tuning the code itself.


Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.subject: Re: Modifying graph colors and visualising figure legends
parts:
New beta release of Rattle (r139) will now use corrplot() for the correlation plots if the Advanced Graphics option is enabled (as it is by default in the beta version). I think the use of filled circles, and the circle size indicating the strength of the correlation and still using colour for the direction of the correlation, together with a legend, as Ramesh requested, looks good.

Beta release can be installed as:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com
